capability.summary: Fetch one URL and report presence of six fixed HTTP security response headers
capability.description: Prefixes scheme-less input with HTTPS, performs a redirect-following GET, and reports which of six recognized header names are present at the final response. The score is only a presence count and does not validate header values or security effectiveness.
capability.problem_space: Coarse single-response inventory of six HTTP security header names; not policy-value validation, vulnerability certification, TLS auditing, CORS analysis, browser behavior simulation, or comprehensive web security testing.

env_requirements: network access to the target and redirect destinations
constraint.io_signature: Input: one required HTTP(S) URL or scheme-less host/path string; output: JSON with final URL, HTTP status, fixed present/missing header sets, and a presence-count score, or a request error.
accepted_inputs: an absolute http:// or https:// URL
a scheme-less host or host/path string that should be fetched over https://
constraint.output_shape: Successful HTTP exchange, including 4xx/5xx: {status: "success", tool: "requests", url: string, status_code: integer, present_security_headers: object, missing_security_headers: string[], score: string}; url is the final response URL, present values are raw strings, and score is `<present count>/6`. Request failure: {status: "error", tool: "requests", url: string, message: string} and exit 1. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON.
limitations: checks presence only for Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; values are not parsed or judged
the score is a six-header presence ratio, not a security grade, vulnerability result, compliance decision, or proof of browser protection
performs a GET with redirects enabled and Requests' default full-response download behavior; there is no method, request-header, redirect-count, body-size, or target-network restriction
uses a 20-second Requests timeout rather than a guaranteed total deadline, treats HTTP error statuses as successful exchanges, and does not inspect CORS or TLS configuration

output_contract.description: JSON presence inventory for six fixed security headers at the final GET response URL, with HTTP status and a non-semantic count score.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: check whether common HTTP security headers are present
inventory six fixed security headers from a URL response

inspect CORS headers or send a preflight OPTIONS request
audit TLS certificates ciphers application vulnerabilities or full web compliance
